overall_summary: Analysis of 47 deduplicated shorts shows extreme performance polarization. Visceral, first-person 'What If You Fell Into...' cosmic survival scenarios and exotic planetary extremes dominate the channel (averaging 800-1,050 views, 15-38 likes, and driving comments). Conversely, generic psychology trivia ('Your Brain Can Create Fake Memories') and repeated uploads ('Why Space Is Completely Silent') consistently stall under 100 views with near-zero engagement. Shorts timed at 19-21 seconds posted between 12:00 and 13:30 UTC capture the highest velocity.

winning_patterns.pattern: First-Person Peril / 'What If You Fell Into...' Hook
winning_patterns.evidence: Titles using 'What If You Fell Into...' (IYuce8vaU3Y: 1,029 views, 38 likes, 2 comments; 8KEl0_pJ_68: 972 views, 18 likes; YlDuGu1vzAg: 823 views, 15 likes; 6pwazIPnOHw: 495 views, 23 likes) outperform channel baseline by 400-800%.
winning_patterns.action: Anchor future space and extreme environment Shorts around immediate bodily stakes and first-person visual descent.

winning_patterns.evidence: Concepts highlighting tangible physical paradoxes like TrES-2b 'Darker Than Coal' (1,028 views, 36 likes) and 'Supersonic Rubies' (723 views, 25 likes) drive top-tier likes-per-view (>3.5%).
winning_patterns.action: Pair planetary extremes with vivid tactile sensations (crushing density, burning cold, exotic precipitation).

weak_patterns.evidence: 'Your Brain Can Create Fake Memories' uploaded across multiple IDs yielded 5, 10, and 53 views with 0 likes; 'Your Brain Is Hiding This From You' received only 38 views.
weak_patterns.action: Pause passive brain trivia; pivot psychology content into high-stakes behavioral survival dilemmas or micro-mysteries.

weak_patterns.evidence: 'Why Space Is Completely Silent' repeated three times degraded from 220 views to 87 and finally 34 views.
weak_patterns.action: Enforce strict fresh-topic verification before rendering to avoid audience fatigue and algorithmic suppression.
